mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the cases when FEDFUNDS is low, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth, as indicated by GDPC1, may lead to weaker corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is below 2% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) combined with falling employment (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production (INDPRO) in a late-cycle expansion may not support equity returns, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO is high in late-cycle but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates may indicate monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising real consumer spending (RSAFS) may boost corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment (UNRATE) may indicate a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates combined with slowing GDP growth may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high and GDPC1 growth slows but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.
